photos.title: Wheelchair-space call button on a bus
photos.note: Kurumaisu-seki sen’yō: for the wheelchair space only. The button itself says お降りの方はこのボタンを押してください, “if you are getting off, please press this button”.
photos.author: Tama998

photos.title: Platform guide at Shin-Ōsaka Station
photos.note: Noriba: where to board. Platforms 13–14 go towards Suita, Ibaraki, Takatsuki and Kyoto; 15–16 towards Ōsaka (Umeda), Sannomiya and Kobe. The red panel lists the limited-express platforms.
photos.author: Starbacks

photos.title: Next-stop display on a bus
photos.note: Tsugi wa Hirota-jinja-mae: next stop, Hirota Shrine. The normal fare (通常運賃) is ¥240 for adults and ¥120 for children.
photos.author: NatsuTV

photos.title: Station sign at Kōsoku-Kobe
photos.note: Kōsoku-Kōbe station, with the neighbouring stations in hiragana: しんかいち (Shinkaichi) one way, はなくま (Hanakuma) and にしもとまち (Nishi-Motomachi) the other.
photos.author: NatsuTV

photos.title: Exit 4 at Karasuma-Marutamachi Station
photos.note: Deguchi: exit. The yellow panel lists what is near this exit; the white signs point to the elevators (エレベーター) and the ticket gates (改札口).
photos.author: HAGAT hOMSZE

photos.title: Departure board on a Hankyu platform
photos.note: Destinations on the board: Tengachaya (天下茶屋), Tenjimbashi-suji Rokuchōme (天神橋筋六丁目), Awaji (淡路) and Ōsaka-Umeda (大阪梅田). 回送 (kaisō) means out of service.
photos.author: MaedaAkihiko

photos.title: Station sign at Nanao
photos.note: Nanao, with the reading ななお and the neighbouring stations とくだ (Tokuda) and わくらおんせん (Wakura Onsen) on the arrows.
photos.author: MaedaAkihiko

photos.title: Destination display on a Keihan train
photos.note: Kaisoku kyūkō: rapid express, bound for Yodoyabashi.
photos.author: NatsuTV

photos.title: Next-station display on the Kobe subway
photos.ja: つぎは 中央市場前
photos.note: Tsugi wa Chūō-shijō-mae: next, Central Market. The right side shows the stations ahead on the way to Misaki Park (御崎公園).
photos.author: NatsuTV

photos.title: Platform screen on the Midōsuji Line
photos.note: Hi-teishōsha: not a low-floor train. The screen warns that on trains marked this way the step between platform and door has not been reduced (ホームとの段差が縮小されていません).
photos.author: 日根野

photos.title: Temporary paving: mind your step
photos.ja: 仮舗装 足もと注意
photos.note: Kari-hosō: temporary road surface; ashimoto chūi: watch your step. Painted on the pavement.
photos.author: Misei sen

photos.title: Cliff warning on a wooded hill
photos.ja: この先は崖、危険！ 立入禁止
photos.note: “Cliff ahead, danger! Keep out.” Below: 約60mもある崖があります, there is a cliff about 60 m high. Furigana over the kanji help children read it; the sign on the left says この先行きどまり, dead end ahead.
photos.author: Nikm

photos.title: No flyers, please
photos.note: Issai o-kotowari shimasu: we refuse it entirely. Above: posting flyers, free papers and other advertising (チラシ・フリーペーパー・勧誘印刷物) without permission; below: in bad cases we call the police at once.
photos.author: Syced

photos.title: Notice at a level crossing
photos.note: Chūi: caution; romen ōtotsu: uneven road surface. Below: お願い しゃ断時間長いので、歩道橋を渡って下さい, “please use the footbridge, as the barrier stays down for a long time”.
photos.author: Hitachi-Train

photos.title: No parties under the cherry trees
photos.note: Enkai wa kinshi desu: parties are prohibited. Put up in the 2022 cherry-blossom season to stop group eating and drinking during the pandemic.
photos.author: Syced

photos.title: Dam-release warning by a river
photos.ja: 危い!! ダムの放流による増水に注意
photos.note: Abunai! Beware of rising water when the dam releases water. Written in simple Japanese with furigana; a siren and a turning red lamp give warning before a release.
photos.author: Kodai Kishi

photos.title: Street-smoking notice in Kyoto
photos.note: Rojō kitsuen: smoking in the street. In the marked areas it costs a ¥1,000 fine (過料, karyō); the notice repeats this in English, Chinese and Korean.
photos.author: HAGAT hOMSZE

photos.title: No urinating
photos.note: Daishōben kinshi: no urinating or defecating. Above: 大小便は犯罪です, it is a crime; below: offenders will be reported to the police and charged ¥50,000 (金5万円を徴収します).
photos.author: Pocsywe

photos.title: Flood warning on a street pole
photos.note: Ōame-ji kansui chūi: beware of flooding in heavy rain. Put up by the Tsurumi public-works office (横浜市鶴見土木事務所).
photos.author: 蒼空かな

photos.title: Climbers’ registration box at a station
photos.note: Tozan todoke: a climbing plan. Hikers leave their route and dates in the box before heading into the mountains.
photos.author: Asasa198

photos.title: Building-plan notice on a site wall
photos.note: Kenchiku keikaku no oshirase: notice of a building plan, required by ward rules before a tall building goes up. This one is for rebuilding the Embassy of Indonesia.
photos.author: Syced

photos.title: River-land permit board
photos.note: Kasen sen’yō kyoka hyōshiki: permit sign for using river land. It lists the purpose (緑地広場, green space), the area and the holder (渋谷区, Shibuya City).
photos.author: Syced

photos.title: History board for a vanished park
photos.note: Shizen-en, “nature garden”: a health park of the Taishō era. The board, put up by the Meguro board of education, tells its story; furigana give the reading of the name.
photos.author: Wadakuramon

photos.title: Plate on a railway bridge
photos.note: Tsunohazu gādo: the Tsunohazu railway bridge on the Chūō Line. お願い (please): if you see a vehicle hit the bridge, contact the railway at once (自動車等が衝突したのを見た方は、至急御連絡下さい).
photos.author: Shin-Nippori

photos.title: Shopping-street gate
photos.ja: 高円寺 純情商店街
photos.note: Kōenji Junjō shōtengai. A shōtengai (商店街) is a local shopping street, often marked by a gate like this.
photos.author: Yoshibay

photos.title: Signpost to walkways and a station
photos.note: Midorigaoka-eki hōkō: towards Midorigaoka Station. The other arms point to two green walkways (緑道, ryokudō) along buried rivers: 呑川本流緑道 and 九品仏川緑道.
photos.author: Mizuhara gumi

photos.title: Road sign to the Yubatake
photos.note: Yubatake, literally “hot-water field”: the steaming spring at the heart of Kusatsu Onsen. The English line reads Hot Water Field.
photos.author: Aspere

photos.title: Route sign on National Route 4
photos.ja: 宇都宮 102km　春日部 26km　三ノ輪 1km
photos.note: Distances to Utsunomiya, Kasukabe and Minowa along National Route 4; place names on road signs come with rōmaji.
photos.author: Taufik

photos.title: Sardine label in Kansai dialect
photos.ja: いわしを食べなあかん！
photos.note: “You’ve got to eat sardines!” なあかん (naakan) is Kansai dialect for なければならない, must. Below, the fish and where it comes from: 石川県, Ishikawa Prefecture.
photos.author: Nils R. Barth

photos.title: Buttons on a tea machine
photos.note: O-yu: hot water; o-cha: tea. Both take the polite prefix お.
photos.author: Nils R. Barth

photos.title: Shop sign: engagement gifts, go and shōgi
photos.ja: 結納セット 碁・将棋
photos.note: Yuinō setto: engagement-gift sets; go and shōgi: the two classic board games. One shop sells both.
photos.author: AUTUMNSNAKE

photos.title: Help yourself
photos.ja: ご自由にお持ち下さい！
photos.note: Go-jiyū ni o-mochi kudasai: please take what you like. A handwritten note on a box of old crockery left on the pavement.
photos.author: Pocsywe

photos.title: Restaurant name board
photos.note: O-ryōri Yamasaki: Yamasaki, Japanese cuisine, brushed in calligraphy on wood. The name itself is written in hiragana.
photos.author: 経済特区

photos.title: Vending-machine corner
photos.note: Jihanki kōnā: vending-machine corner. 自販機 is short for 自動販売機.
photos.author: Hippietrail

photos.title: Shrine name pillar
photos.note: Akiba Jinja. A stone pillar carved with the shrine’s name (社号標, shagōhyō) stands at the entrance and is read top to bottom.
photos.author: 先従隗始

photos.title: Viewpoint sign at Amanohashidate
photos.note: Nihon sankei Amanohashidate: Amanohashidate, one of the Three Views of Japan.
photos.author: RED COMET J. P.

photos.title: 1930s railway travel poster
photos.ja: 奇勝の蘇洞門 小濱の海水浴
photos.note: Read right to left, as on many pre-war signs: the wonderful rocks of Sotomo, sea bathing at Obama. Issued by the Ōsaka and Nagoya railway bureaus (大阪鐵道局・名古屋鐵道局).
photos.author: Japanese Government Railways

photos.title: 1937 beer advert
photos.note: Asahi beer, written right to left as was usual before the war. 一等國の一等品: first-class goods of a first-class nation. From Dai-Nippon Brewery’s Nagoya branch.
photos.author: 大日本麦酒株式会社名古屋支店
